answer: Persistent work-credit ledger. Each new identity starts with zero credits; earning credits requires completing tasks whose outputs are later audited by unrelated identities. Auditors reject low-quality work probabilistically, so clones must fund real labor to reach a usable credit balance. A sybil cluster needs N times the audit-surviving output, and a ferrous hardware token bound to one ledger slot caps parallel registration. Attackers cannot find a haven of unaudited tasks; every clone pays the same marginal labor cost, making duplication strictly negative-EV.
